punchline: Lynch recommended Chrysler on television while his relatives asked if he knew it was going bankrupt.
thirty_sec: In October 1982 Chrysler was Peter Lynch's biggest holding, and he recommended it on television at around $10 a share. Relatives and friends asked how he could, since the company was supposed to be going bankrupt. Congress had guaranteed $1.5 billion of its loans in 1979, and Chrysler repaid them in 1983, about seven years early. Lynch said it worked out fine, and he recommended it again in 1990.
